purpose: Correct propaganda-centric framing and model TSPU-like centralized in-path infrastructure primarily as a military-operational control surface over the public digital environment, with propaganda/information influence as one downstream exploitation layer rather than the defining function.

russian_official_context: Russia's 2021 National Security Strategy explicitly states that information space is being developed as a new sphere of warfare and calls for development of forces and means of information confrontation.
Russia's 2021 international information security policy explicitly treats ICT use in the military-political sphere as a national/international security issue.

The sovereign-Internet architecture created a state monitoring/control center and mandatory operator-side control infrastructure for resilience/security and centralized intervention in public-network behavior.
strategic_basis.claim_limit: Official Russian documents describe information-security and information-confrontation concepts broadly; they do not by themselves prove TSPU was designed as an offensive military weapon or that exported deployments are under Russian command.

operational_mode_stack.function: Remove ordinary public-network connectivity for a selected area, access class or service category.
operational_mode_stack.strategic_effect: Public-network-dependent coordination ceases rather than merely becoming observable.

operational_mode_stack.function: Preserve only approved/local/state-selected services while broader external connectivity is denied.
operational_mode_stack.strategic_effect: Creates simultaneous communications denial and information-environment substitution without a total visible blackout.

operational_mode_stack.function: Block/throttle selected protocols, destinations, applications or circumvention surfaces while leaving the rest of the network functional.
operational_mode_stack.strategic_effect: Can selectively remove external command-support, media, cloud or coordination dependencies without collapsing all civilian services.

operational_mode_stack.function: Central policy influence over routing, DNS or in-path enforcement can alter where traffic is allowed to go or which path it inherits.
operational_mode_stack.strategic_effect: Distribution-layer leverage over many downstream users and possibility of moving traffic into a controlled filtering jurisdiction, as historically observed in occupied Ukrainian networks.
operational_mode_stack.claim_limit: TSPU alone does not imply arbitrary global BGP control; route effects require separate operator/transit evidence.

operational_mode_stack.function: For traffic still allowed to traverse the controlled public path, flow-level metadata and behavioral patterns may remain visible even when payload content is encrypted.
operational_mode_stack.strategic_effect: Potential situational-awareness/intelligence value from communication-pattern changes, but not automatic decryption or troop identification.

operational_mode_stack.function: After external/open sources are denied or degraded, state/aligned information services can occupy a larger relative share of the remaining information environment.
operational_mode_stack.strategic_effect: Propaganda becomes more effective because distribution competition has been reduced; propaganda is an exploitation layer, not the core network-control function.

juxtapose_mirror.reference_principle: LEARN WHERE TO LOOK; NEVER LEARN WHAT IS TRUE.
juxtapose_mirror.defensive_parallel: JUXTAPOSE treats fresh measurement, path availability, shared failure domains and policy drift as authoritative for communications resilience in DDIL environments. The threat mirror is that a centralized network controller can deliberately create or move those failure domains for public-network users.
juxtapose_mirror.key_difference: JUXTAPOSE seeks resilient authorized paths; a hostile control surface seeks to make selected paths unavailable, unreliable or policy-constrained.
juxtapose_mirror.important_constraint: JUXTAPOSE cannot create connectivity where all physical/authorized edges are unavailable. Therefore a sufficiently broad deny/allowlist regime on the only available public path can create a true communication barrier rather than merely a degraded route-selection problem.

friendly_force_and_partner_risk.first_order: COMMUNICATION DENIAL for any workflow dependent on the affected public mobile/Internet path.
friendly_force_and_partner_risk.second_order: SELECTIVE SERVICE DENIAL can remove cloud, messaging, mapping, developer, media or coordination services while preserving approved local services.
friendly_force_and_partner_risk.third_order: OBSERVABILITY/traffic analysis matters for whatever communications remain on the controlled path.
friendly_force_and_partner_risk.fourth_order: INFORMATION ISOLATION can reduce external situational awareness and increase relative exposure to aligned narratives.
friendly_force_and_partner_risk.boundary: Independent tactical radio, protected satellite, dedicated military networks and other communications not traversing the controlled public network are outside the automatic-effect claim.

historical_progression: Crimea/Donbas 2014: seize broadcast/cable distribution and replace sources.
Occupied Ukraine 2022+: seize frequencies and reroute public Internet through Russian-controlled networks, importing Russian filtering conditions.
Russia 2025-2026: regional mobile shutdowns plus officially confirmed deny-except-allowlist operation.

Candidate future risk: externally deployed centralized network-control infrastructure could reproduce denial/isolation functions without requiring physical seizure of each local transmitter, but external Russian command is not established.
threat_chain_if_external_control_ever_pr: loss of ordinary external communications for public-network-dependent actors
degraded foreign situational awareness and partner coordination
narrative exploitation of the resulting information vacuum

why_this_is_military_relevant_without_ca.reason: The capability directly affects communications availability, information access, operational dependence on civilian telecom infrastructure and crisis-time coordination.
why_this_is_military_relevant_without_ca.official_context: Russian strategy treats information space as a warfare/security domain and explicitly calls for information-confrontation capabilities.
why_this_is_military_relevant_without_ca.claim_ceiling: Military relevance is established as a risk category; offensive military employment of foreign TSPU systems remains unproven without command/control, deployment and event evidence.

agency_translation.ODNI_FMIC: Model as strategic information-and-communications control capability that could enable coercion, malign influence and denial if external command/deployment bridges exist.
agency_translation.CISA: Model as foreign public-network dependency, denial/allowlist, routing and service-reachability risk rather than as a propaganda issue.
agency_translation.FBI: Relevant where U.S. persons, companies, infrastructure or foreign-influence operations are affected by covert/remote control or hostile denial.
agency_translation.STATE_CDP_CFIMI: Relevant as open-Internet, partner resilience and foreign-information-manipulation risk when network control and narrative exploitation reinforce each other.

hard_falsifiers: No shared external control plane -> no basis for coordinated Russian foreign activation claim.
Foreign deployment controlled solely by host-state authority -> local censorship/sovereign control case, not Russian command.
Independent communications remain functional -> do not claim universal military C2 denial.
No selective survival of aligned services -> do not infer source-substitution strategy from a generic infrastructure outage.
Provider-side failure explains reachability loss -> prefer provider RCA over external-control speculation.
best_current_claim: TSPU should be analyzed primarily as a centralized public-network control surface with direct operational relevance to denial, isolation, allowlisting, selective service reachability and remaining-traffic observability. Propaganda is a downstream exploitation layer that becomes more powerful after communication and information-distribution control is achieved. Russia has demonstrated domestic shutdown/allowlist capability and historical conflict-time distribution control, but public evidence does not establish Russian remote command of sovereign foreign deployments or a synchronized external activation network.
